chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Abī Naṣr, from some of our companions, said:
Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “The woman who has despaired of menstruation—her limit is fifty years.”

key_terms.الْمَحِيضِ: menstruation; the monthly bleeding relevant to ritual purity laws
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةُ: the woman; the subject of the legal ruling
key_terms.حَدُّهَا: her limit; the fixed legal boundary or criterion
key_terms.خَمْسُونَ: fifty; the specified age in the ruling
key_terms.سَنَةً: years; the unit of age intended in the ruling
key_terms.يَئِسَتْ: has despaired; meaning she has ceased to expect menstruation

ai.seo_question: At what age is a woman considered to have despaired of menstruation according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the age at which a woman is regarded as having despaired of menstruation. It serves as a fiqh-based criterion in the laws related to menstruation and ritual purity.
